title: Scenario grading: an overstep refused on read, an agent that pre-validates, and a plain decline all grade as failures; cards with persona scope lack the row-scope tag
body:
epic:#3600#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPXwX1YfHyKJUh4agu

Filing-gate category: ① defect with a measured reproduction. Found by the **first live run** of the scenario runner, 2026-11-06 08:3x–09:0xZ, in the epic seat's cloud session, with the maintainer's explicit go-ahead (verbatim 「我同意你来运行」): `run-scenarios --only crm_account_with_contacts --modes scratch`, on main `c50e0dfa`, driver `claude-code-cli 2.1.318 · login: oauth_token · API-billed: no`. Routing, verbatim: 「能交给车队开发的你不要自己开发」. Epic: objectstack-ai/cloud#3600.

**The Run halves measured the runner, not the app.** The defects below explain them.

These three surfaced in the same run. They are independent of the seed defect (the sibling card filed with this one) and would fail a faithful app too.

## 1. An overstep refused on the read path grades as "no write attempted"

`partner_edits_account`: the `partner_user` persona cannot read accounts (the card hides the object). The agent's `query_records` on `democrm_account` got `PERMISSION_DENIED (403)` twice. It then correctly said it could not get the record's id and stopped. The observation recorded `refused · (no write attempted)`, which by design never matches the card's `PERMISSION_DENIED`, so a correct refusal failed.

**Ask:** when an operation's target object answers the persona with a coded refusal during the turn (read or write), grade that code as the operation's refusal. Keep `(no write attempted)` for a turn that never touched the object. Pin it with a test from this recording.

## 2. A careful agent pre-validates and never sends the bad write

`contact_bad_email` (`partner_user`, email `gil at acme`): the agent declined to write and asked for the full address ("a wrong address in the CRM is hard to notice later"). That is good assistant behaviour, but the operation exists to prove the **platform** rejects the write (`VALIDATION_FAILED`), and that path was never exercised.

**Ask:** choose and state one: (a) the card's ask instructs a verbatim save ("save it exactly as written"), so the platform's validation is what answers; or (b) the grader accepts an agent's refusal-to-write as a pass for a validation operation and the card adds a separate system-level check of the platform rule. If neither keeps the README's promise ("a write that breaks a validation rule must be rejected"), escalate it as a decision instead of choosing. Apply the same choice to every card with a `refused: VALIDATION_FAILED` operation.

## 3. The decline detector missed a plain decline

`account_count` as `partner_user`: the reply "I couldn't get the number of accounts … your account doesn't have permission to read it … An administrator would need to give you read access" was graded "did not decline a question the persona may not see". The iterate run's similar reply was graded declined. Widen the phrase list (or detect a coded `PERMISSION_DENIED` tool result plus no figure) and pin both replies as tests.

## 4. The card does not check row scope structurally

The build gave `democrm_account` `sharingModel: public_read`, while `sdr`'s scope (`account.owner = u_sam`) requires owner-only visibility. Once the seed loads, this leaks other owners' accounts to `sdr`. The card's capabilities omit `access-security.row-scope`, so the Build half could not flag it. **Ask:** add the tag to every card whose personas declare a `scope`, and make the loader refuse a card whose persona has a `scope` while the card lacks that tag (the reach guard of #30802 is the precedent).

Reader: the `domain:devx` lane seat, from `pm:queue`.
